title: POC kickoff alignment and blocker burnup
content:
Purpose: quick working doc for customer kickoff, alignment on scope, and a living blocker burnup for week-by-week ops. Informal notes + explicit next actions for SEs and Eng.

Context and customer snapshot:
- Customer: BrightEdge Analytics (data platform vendor), evaluating Redwood Dedicated for realtime summarization pipelines. Sensitive PCI adjacent data; leaning toward Private/VPC. Wants 95th percentile latency < 350ms for 512-token windows, and cost targets that fit within 3x current CPU baseline.
- Primary contact: Allison Mercer (BrightEdge), infra lead Dan Cho, ML eng TBD.
- Evaluation length: 6 weeks (pilot -> canary -> production mirror)
- Key constraints: VPC peering allowed but no shared tenancy; audit log retention required; limited to 4x A100-style GPUs during pilot.

Kickoff goals (what we must leave the meeting with):
- Agreed acceptance criteria (performance, cost, security checkpoint list)
- Owner assignment for every top-level ticket
- Agreed timeline for week 0..5 and nightly checkpoint time (15:00 PT)
- Known blockers catalogued and prioritized

Attendees (internal): Maya Chen (SE, owner), Rafiq Ahmed (Solutions Lead), Olivia Park (Platform eng liaison), Samir Patel (Security), Diego Vargas (SRE). External: Allison Mercer, Dan Cho.

Kickoff agenda (45m):
- 0-5m: quick intros + scope check
- 5-12m: customer primary use case walkthrough (BrightEdge LLM summarizer)
- 12-22m: infrastructure constraints (VPC, private endpoints, KMS)
- 22-32m: perf targets, dataset footprint, test harness
- 32-40m: success metrics + rollback criteria
- 40-45m: action items and owners

Acceptance criteria (draft — needs Allison signoff):
- Performance: p95 < 350ms, p99 < 700ms for 512 tokens under 50 rps sustained with burst to 200 rps for 30s.
- Quality: output ROUGE-L >= baseline on internal evaluation prompt set (redwood: hosted-evals/brightedge-v1)
- Security: VPC peering with private-control-plane, KMS integration for key usage, logs forwarded to customer SIEM (splunk) with retention 90 days.
- Operational: auto-failover to hosted model variant within 300s on Dedicated capacity outage; rollback plan validated in lab.

High-level timeline (living — weeks relative to kickoff):
- Week 0 (kickoff week): environment access validated, sample payloads & prompts ingested, small smoke runs (1-5 rps)
- Week 1: baseline latency tests with unquantized model, initial KV cache configuration, first regression eval run
- Week 2: batching and service-level params tuning (max batch size, batching window), run A/B vs hosted variant
- Week 3: quantization profile test (int8/4-bit experiments), memory pressure checks, and cost modeling
- Week 4: canary rollout to 10% customer traffic, monitoring dashboards and alerts validated
- Week 5: production mirror test, finalize SLA language and runbook
- Week 6: handoff and optional extension to dedicated capacity commit negotiation

Weekly checkpoints and owners (short):
- Environment access and secrets: Samir Patel
- Test harness + scripts: Diego Vargas
- Perf tuning (batching/cache): Olivia Park
- Quantization experiments + evals: Maya Chen
- Customer comms and acceptance: Rafiq Ahmed

Blocker burnup (log):
- B1 (2025-09-03): VPC peering request stuck with customer network team — severity: high. Impact: cannot test Private plan. Owner: Allison/Dan. Action: escalate via SE+AM. Status: open.
- B2 (2025-09-04): Customer cannot forward logs to Splunk due to proxy rules. Owner: Samir. Workaround: collect logs via S3 sink. Status: mitigation in progress.
- B3 (2025-09-05): GPU quota limited to 2 during pilot (customer side). Owner: Maya. Impact: throughput testing constrained. Status: open, compensating plan: reduce concurrency and increase test time windows.
- B4 (2025-09-07): Eval dataset contains PII flagged in review — compliance hold. Owner: Rafiq. Status: investigating redaction pipeline.

Open decisions (requires customer/PM):
- D1: Is strict KMS/HSM required for pilot or only for production? (customer leaning production-only)
- D2: Acceptable cost threshold at 50 rps baseline — customer has internal budget target that would require 20% or more optimization vs default config.
- D3: Canary routing policy — weighted traffic vs header-based routing.

Test plan highlights:
- Smoke cases: 5 payload shapes (short, medium, long, multi-turn stateful, function-calling payload)
- Load testing: synthetic rps generator + recorded user traces from BrightEdge (sanitized)
- Evals: 3 prompt suites (summarize, extractive QA, conversational followups). Use Redwood-eval harness, track regressions.
- Metrics to capture: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, utilization per GPU, cache hit ratio, cost-per-1k-tokens estimate.

Safety/regulatory quick notes:
- Customer requires data residency to stay in us-east-1 for pilot. Ensure all pilot infra in region.
- Audit trail: retain request/response metadata only; redact user text for compliance during evals.

Rollout & rollback playbook (short):
- Canary step: push model variant to Dedicated pool, route 10% traffic for 24h. If p95 or error rate crosses threshold (5x baseline) -> automatically roll back to hosted fallback.
- Automatic fallback config: route by region and tier; fallback target: hosted-inference/compat-1.0
- Manual rollback: SE opens incident, scales Dedicated down, flips routing, and triggers customer alert.

Runbook snippets (to later copy to Redwood Console):
- Alert thresholds: p95 > 400ms sustained for 10m; error rate > 1% for 5m -> page oncall SRE.
- Investigations: check KV cache hit ratio, batch sizes, and GPU utilization.

Immediate next actions (24-72h):
- Rafiq: confirm customer acceptance criteria and sign written note to proceed. (Due: 2025-09-05)
- Samir: draft temp log-forwarding plan via S3 and get security approval. (Due: 2025-09-06)
- Maya: prepare quantization test script + baseline run and upload to GH. (Due: 2025-09-06)
- Diego: provision test harness in us-east-1, seed sample traces. (Due: 2025-09-04)

Notes to self (choppy, copy-paste candidate for deck):
- Keep experiments small — quantize one layer at a time, measure perplexity drift
- Try prefix caching for repeated-ish queries — big wins for cost
- Demo to Allison: 30s end-to-end from code to inference via dedicated cluster
- Temp: ask infra if we can provision 1 extra GPU for 48h as buffer during week2

Risks + mitigations (short bullets):
- Risk: network approvals delay. Mitigation: parallelize with hosted fallback testing; do quality evals on hosted while peering is negotiated.
- Risk: cost overshoot with naive batch sizes. Mitigation: run Redwood Optimize suggestions and stop tests at cost threshold.
- Risk: Eval regression on quantized model. Mitigation: keep unquantized baseline and automatic comparison suite.

Appendix: useful links / snippets
- Quick test harness command: python infra/load_runner.py --config brightedge-smoke.yaml --rps 10 --duration 600
- GH PR with initial scripts: https://github.com/redwood-inference/poc-scripts/pull/78
- Confluence: POC checklist template: https://confluence.redwood.tech/display/SE/POC-templates

Questions for next sync:
- Can customer share CI/CD access pattern for their summarizer? (helps automate canary)
- Are there third-party libs that block quantization (custom ops)?

Status: draft — will refine after first 48h of pickup and push final acceptance criteria into a signed doc.
